8.need-data: This stage uses your data and stages 1 to 7: load your data and complete them first.

opens.title: What gets opened
opens.test: The test set stage 6 sealed: {n} rows, seal {sello}.
opens.train: Stage 7's winner, {ganador}, is fitted on the {n} training rows and predicts the test set.
opens.once: The test set opens once. What you see here can no longer be used to pick another model unnoticed: if you open it again with a different setup, the notebook labels it.
opens.count: You've already opened it with {count} different setups.
opens.seal-bad: The seal your table gives today isn't the one stage 6 recorded: the test set doesn't open. Check stage 6.
opens.cannot: Something is missing to open the test set: stage 7's winner, its metric, or columns in «use».

open.loading: Getting Python ready in your browser…
open.measuring: Fitting the winner on the training set and measuring the test set…
open.cancelled: You cancelled: the test set wasn't opened and nothing was recorded.
open.error: The test set couldn't be opened ({motivo}); nothing was recorded.
open.note: It runs in your browser: neither the test set nor the rest of your data travels to any server.

measure.title: The measurement on the test set
measure.no-rule: In stage 5 you said there's no current rule: there's nothing to compare it with.
measure.how: With stage 1's costs and threshold. The interval resamples {conglomerado} {b} times with a fixed seed: the same file always gives the same interval.

cluster.unidad: whole units (rows from the same unit aren't independent)
cluster.fecha: whole dates (rows from the same date aren't independent)

measure.optimism: Selection score (stage 7): {seleccion} in {metrica}. On the test set, the same metric gives {prueba}.
measure.optimism-none: No optimism: the winner did as well or better on the test set than at selection.

segments.title: Error by segment
segments.global: Over the whole test set, the winner costs {costo} per 100 decisions.
segments.none: No segment has enough support: the test set can't be read in parts.
segments.none-worse: No segment with support does worse than the whole test set: there is no worst segment to mark.
segments.empty: There are no segments to read: no date, no categories with 2 to 8 values, and no numeric columns in «use».
segments.rule-cases: Minimum support: {filas} rows and {casos} cases of the less frequent class. A segment without support is shown, but it's never the worst. It's a convention of this program, not a statistical test.
segments.rule: Minimum support: {filas} rows. A segment without support is shown, but it's never the worst. It's a convention of this program, not a statistical test.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.what-binaria: What the model said about «action needed», against what happened, in equal-width bins.
calibration.what-multiclase: How confident the model was in the class it chose, against whether it was right, in equal-width bins.
calibration.brier: Brier: {brier}. Always saying the base rate would give {base}. Lower is better.
calibration.reading: When it says between {desde} and {hasta}%, it happens in {observado}% of {n} cases.
calibration.reading-none: No bin reaches {n} cases: the curve can't be put into words.
calibration.sin-probabilidades: The winner doesn't give probabilities: its calibration can't be measured. The gate accepts that.
calibration.no-aplica: When estimating a quantity there are no probabilities to calibrate: it doesn't apply.
calibration.measures: This stage measures calibration; it doesn't fix the model.

worst.title: The worst cases
worst.note: The {n} most expensive mistakes on the test set. They're shown only on your screen: they aren't saved in the notebook, aren't exported, and never leave your browser.
worst.region: The worst cases on the test set
worst.empty: No row of the test set had a cost above zero.

pattern.label: Your failure pattern
pattern.help: In your own words: what do the worst cases have in common? For example, «it fails with new customers from the web channel». Up to {max} characters. It stays in the notebook for the model card in stage 10.

check.clase_rara: Less frequent class on the test set
check.base_bajo: Baseline: low end of the interval
check.base_alto: Baseline: high end of the interval
check.regla_costo: Your current rule's cost per decision
check.regla_bajo: Your rule: low end of the interval
check.regla_alto: Your rule: high end of the interval
check.seg_casos: Less frequent class cases, per segment
check.prueba_metrica: The league metric on the test set
check.ganador_bajo: Winner: low end of the interval
check.ganador_alto: Winner: high end of the interval
check.aperturas: Distinct openings of the test set
check.peor_exceso: Worst segment's extra cost per decision
check.seg_costo: Winner's cost per decision, per segment
check.prueba_pos: Positive rows in the test set
check.regla_vp: Your rule: alerts that are right in the test set
check.regla_fp: Your rule: false alarms in the test set
check.tabla_umbrales: Right and false alerts, by threshold
